svg.aria-label: One thread of the tiled attention kernel, thread 45 = warp 1 lane 13. It owns rows 20 to 23 of the tile. Step 1: it computes a 4 by 4 patch of the score chunk from 4 whole rows of Q and 4 whole columns of K transpose. Steps 2 to 6: the 8 lanes that share those rows combine row max and row sum with three xor shuffles, exponentiate in place, rescale the output, and write P to shared. Step 7: it reads 4 whole rows of P, including values from the other 7 lanes, and 8 columns of V, accumulating a 4 by 8 patch of O in registers.
svg.text: one thread of the tiled kernel: threadIdx 45 = warp 1, lane 13 -> laneRow 1, laneCol 5
Br = 64, Bc = 32, d = 64, 128 threads. It owns tile rows 20-23 for the whole kernel (rows = warpId*16 + laneRow*4 + i).
16 dot products of length 64, no other thread involved
S rows 20-23 of this chunk, zoomed: 8 lanes share them
hold the row's chunk max (then sum)
s is now P, in place
P patch -> Pts in shared, sync
everything per row is a warp shuffle:
j = 0..31: the whole chunk, not just its 4 keys
same rows, the other 7 lanes of its group
m, l, o: live for the whole kernel
= 56 floats of state (+ a[4], b[4] operand fragments)
loop over chunks: steps 1-7 each time. after the last chunk: O[row_i][col_c] = o[i][c] / l[i] -- 8 float4 stores.
